notes: The manual does not name specific breadboard holes. The LED goes in column 1, with the anode in the top bank ('left of the ravine') and the cathode in the bottom bank. The exact rows (e, f, g, h) and the resistor's second column (5) are my choices.

The 3V3 jumper's male end is in the same column-bank as the LED anode (1t). The resistor's first leg shares the cathode strip (1b). The GND jumper's male end shares the resistor's second-leg strip (5b).
For jumper-wire-mf I assumed port 'a' is the male end (into the breadboard) and port 'b' is the female end (onto the Pi pin).
The manual says only '3V3' and 'GND' without a pin number, so I used 3V3.1 and GND.1 on the Pi.

The first image shows the flat edge on the LED, which marks the cathode. The LED is polarized (A to 3V3 side, C toward the resistor and GND). The breadboard image shows the ravine and rows; no further parts were seen.
The MCP servers claude.ai Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive need authorization through the claude.ai connector settings. They were not needed for this task.
